I've been interested in linguistics and language for a long time and already have a book on conlang (Mark Rosenfelder's Language Construction Kit) that touches on some basic linguistics, but I'd like some in-depth explanations and such about the subjects mentioned in said book... or just any basic-level books to help me truly kick off my interest and knowledge in this subject.

Thanks in advance for all the recommendations!
I'm looking to start reading up on linguistics. Which books would you recommend me starting out with?

I know this is several months old but perhaps the OP wishes for more suggestions, or someone stumbles upon this link looking for more suggestions. So, with that:

  • David J. Peterson's The Art of Language Invention
  • Hayes' Introductory Phonology
  • Mark Rosenfelder's The Conlanger's Lexipedia
  • A Course in Phonetics by Peter Ladefoged and Keith Johnson
  • Mark Aronoff's What is Morphology
  • Andrew Carnie's Syntax: A Generative Introduction

For more on writing systems, Geoffrey Sampson's Writing Systems: A Linguistic Introduction, Henry Rodgers' Writing Systems: A Linguistic Approach, and The World's Writing Systemsare great additions.

There is also the Advanced version of the Language Construction Kit by Mark Rosenfelder available.
